section: Accidental Deaths and Suicides in India 1994
title: ACCIDENTAL DEATHS & SUICIDES IN INDIA - 1994 N.C.R.B. - 42 1.4.6.1 Less fatality of females may be ascribed to their lesser exposure to outdoor hazards. However, higher percentage of female deaths due to 'Fire' could be attributed to their almost whole time engagements in domestic activities specially in the kitchen involving high exposure to fire hazards. The following table indicates some of the industries where females employees are higher in number than their male counterparts. Although specific number of females dying due to fire in these industries was not available nevertheless it would not be wrong to assume that they would be more vulnerable to such accidents if engaged in fire prone activities.
